content:
What do the "last days of human dominance" look like?

(This is assuming that a *permanent* global stop to AI development does not happen)

First, recall my definition of AGI:

AGI is AI that is powerful enough that if you were to upload it into robot bodies, and all humans suddenly disappeared, it would be able to independently continue civilization.

Why this definition, and not something simpler like "AI that can do 90% of economic tasks at median human level"? Because I think this definition captures the core thing that makes AGI "not just a tool", that make it uniquely powerful and unsettling:

In a "on-the-ground" near-term sense, it means that no specific single job is truly safe from automation. Some jobs might have temporary human advantage, but if they needed to, AIs could eventually figure their way around anything.

But also in a more high-level megapolitical sense, once we have AGI, the fact that it's humans who are masters of the Earth, and not robots, becomes a mere historical contingency (we have the property rights and the master keys to the guns, bots don't), and not an inherent result of bots having any fundamental limitation that we do not have. Even if technology were to advance no further, over centuries and millennia as the world continues to do a random walk constantly restructuring its political organization, there is no guarantee that eventually bots would not be on top - and then win permanently due to their greater ability to mass produce themselves. So AGI, defined as I define it, is a "point of no return" that merits great caution.

content:
中国のAI企業「Moonshot AI」の創業者が、
最新モデル「Kimi K3」について
約40分間のマスター講座を公開してる🔥
👇
「なぜ中国のAI企業は、OpenAIやAnthropicよりも圧倒的に低いコストで高性能モデルを開発できるのか」
その裏側を開発者本人が
かなり具体的に解説しているんだけど　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　

ざっくり動画を要約すると
Kimi K3が狙っているのは
ChatGPTやClaudeの廉価版ではなく

コーディング、長文処理、ツール操作、エージェント機能など、実際の業務で使われる領域において
OpenAIやAnthropicの最上位モデルと
正面から競争することです

特に注目すべきなのが
モデルの性能だけでなく
「性能を出すために必要なコスト」の考え方

・限られた計算資源をどこに使うのか 
・学習データをどう設計するのか 
・推論時のコストをどう抑えるのか 
・モデルをエージェントとしてどう動かすのか 
・高性能を維持したまま価格をどこまで下げられるのか

Kimi K3は、こうした部分を徹底的に
最適化することで、低コストでも
最前線のモデルと戦える
設計を目指している

これまで高性能AIを使うには、
高額なAPI料金や月額課金をしか
選択肢がなかった

しかし、中国企業が同等クラスの
性能を大幅に安い価格あるいは無料に
近い形で提供し始めた。

OpenAIやAnthropicにとって怖いのは、
Kimi K3がベンチマークで
少し勝つことではありません。

「十分に高性能なAIが、圧倒的に安く使える」

という選択肢が世界中に広がることです。

企業がAIモデルを選ぶとき
必ずしも世界最高性能である必要はありません

性能がトップモデルの90〜95％でも、
料金が数分の1で、利用制限が緩く、
エージェントを大量に動かせるなら
実務ではそちらが選ばれる可能性があります

特にAIエージェント時代では、
1回の回答品質だけではなく、

「何回モデルを動かせるか」 
「何体のエージェントを並列稼働できるか」 
「1つのタスクに何度試行錯誤させられるか」

が重要になります。

つまり、低コストであること
自体が性能の一部になる

高価なモデルを1回だけ動かすより、
安価で優秀なモデルを10回動かして
生成・検証・修正を繰り返した方が
最終成果物の品質が
高くなるケースも増えて来ている

Kimi K3は、まさにこの市場を狙っています。
しかも今回の40分間の解説では
単なる宣伝ではなく
中国のAI企業がどのように計算コストを抑え
モデル性能を高め、OpenAIやAnthropicとの
差を縮めようとしているのかが語られている

中国の低コストAIモデルがなぜ
急速に強くなっているのかを理解するには
現時点で最も分かりやすい解説の一つです

無料で視聴できる内容としては
正直かなり濃い。

AI業界がこれから、

「米国の高性能・高価格モデル」 
　　vs 
「中国の高性能・低価格モデル」

という構図に進んでいく
可能性を感じる

AIを使っている人、AIサービスを作っている人
これからAIエージェントを
大量運用したい人は必見の内容だった

40分あるけど
無料のマスタークラスだと
思って見る価値があり👇

最新の動画生成モデル「LTX-2.3」をComfyUIでフル活用するための、実用的な攻略法を紹介します！✨
長尺動画の生成でよく起こる「キャラクターの顔が途中で変わってしまう問題」や「VRAM不足でのエラー」をスマートに回避する知見が詰まっていますよ。

💡 ハードウェアの賢い最適化
公式の推奨環境はA100などの超ハイスペックGPUですが、RTX 5090や4090といった一般的なGPUでも「FP8」や「GGUF」といった量子化（モデルデータを圧縮して軽量化する技術）を適用すれば、高解像度で快適に動作します！
VRAMが16GB前後のカードでも、設定を最適化することで現実的な速度で生成できるようになりますね。

👗 キャラクターの一貫性を保つプロンプト術
動画が進むにつれてキャラクターが徐々に別人になってしまう現象を防ぐには、プロンプトの設計が重要です。
顔立ちや髪型、服装などの「アイデンティティ（外見）」を記述するテキストは全プロンプトで完全に固定（ロック）しておき、動かすアクションやカメラワークのみを書き換える手法が非常に有効です！
さらに、承認済みのフレームを「開始フレーム」として視覚的に参照させることで、時間的な一貫性が劇的に向上しますよ。

🎬 賢い分割ワークフロー
メモリ不足によるクラッシュを防ぎつつ長尺動画を作るには、短いクリップに分割して生成し、後処理で動画ツールを使って結合するのが安全です。
マシンスペックの限界に挑むよりも、クリップの長さ、精度（FP16かFP8か）、解像度のバランスを丁寧に見極めることこそが、ハイクオリティな映像制作の近道になります！

「生成中にパソコンを閉じちゃったらどうするの？」という心配も不要です！
発行される「batch_id」はセッションを跨いでも維持される永続的なIDなので、ネットが途切れたり画面を閉じたりしても、後からちゃんと生成結果（get_batch_output）をまとめて回収できます。非同期での大規模タスク管理にめちゃくちゃ強い仕様ですね！

さらに、単に「処理完了」とするのではなく、データが物理的にストレージに保存されてダウンロードできる状態かを厳密に判定する「ready」ステータス管理（get_batch_status）も備わっています。これでエラーを未然に防ぎ、無駄な通信コストもカットできます！

content:
【低VRAMでも4Kアップスケール！SeedVR2とnative int8 convrotの圧倒的実力】

ComfyUIの超強力なカスタムノード「SeedVR2」がとっても便利で驚きました！✨

ポイントは「native int8 convrot」という量子化技術です。
量子化というのは、モデルのデータを8ビット整数に変換して軽量化し、推論速度をグッと高める技術のこと。これにより画質をキープしながら、GPUのビデオメモリ（VRAM）消費を大幅に削減してくれます。

これがあれば、普通は重くて諦めてしまいそうな「1024pxから4096pxへの4倍高解像度化」が、ノートPCなどの限られたリソースでも快適に行えちゃいます！

用途に合わせて使い分けられるモデル構成も魅力的ですね。
・3B：スピードと省メモリを最優先！
・7B：高精細で美しいクオリティを追求！
・7B Sharp：輪郭をより鮮明にくっきり見せたい時に最適！

さらに「ema_vae_fp16」のVAEと、スケジューラー「euler, simple」を組み合わせる推奨構成のおかげで、量子化特有のノイズや色崩れもしっかり防げます。
高い機材を用意しなくても、手軽にハイクオリティな動画や画像を作れるのはクリエイターにとって大助かりです！

Every company sits on a mountain of data. Almost nobody outside the data team can actually use it.

Marketing wants to know which campaign drove signups. Sales wants churn by region for last quarter. And every time, the answer is the same: "Let me write a query and get back to you."

Someone got tired of being that bottleneck. So they built a way around it.

A tool where anyone — not just the people who know SQL — can open a dashboard, ask a real question, and get a real answer in seconds. No tickets. No waiting on the data team. No learning a query language just to see a number.

It's called Metabase. And it's open source.

Point it at your database and it's already generating charts and dashboards, no setup marathon required. People who do know SQL get a full editor for the hard stuff. Everyone else gets Metabot, an AI that writes the query for them.

Then it keeps going: build governed data models with tracked dependencies, get alerted the second a metric moves, push reports to Slack or email on autopilot, version your work like actual code, and embed the whole thing inside your own product.

48.3k stars. 264 million Docker pulls. Over 500 contributors shipping on it constantly.

The core is fully open source under AGPL, self-hosted for free, forever. There's a managed cloud and enterprise tier if you'd rather not run it yourself. Either way, the tool people used to wait days for is now something anyone on the team can just open and use.

title: Studios, Labels and Scholars Say the Fifth Circuit Botched Vetter
content: Five new amicus briefs urge the Supreme Court to undo the Fifth Circuit’s worldwide-reversion rule, warning it would sow international chaos while quietly stripping foreign creators of the very rights it claims to expand. The Supreme Court justices are on summer recess, but a stack of copyright briefs will be waiting for them when they get back. On Thursday, five separate amicus briefs landed in support of certiorari in BMG Rights Management v. Vetter , the Fifth Circuit headscratcher holding that a U.S. work carries a single copyright that “extends internationally.” BMG, joined by the major labels’ publishing arms, petitioned for cert in June , after buying out the defendant’s copyright interest in “Double Shot (Of My Baby’s Love),” the song at the center of the case known below as Vetter v. Resnik . They’re asking the Court to overturn a ruling that lets creators invoke American law to recapture rights not just here, but all over the globe. The amici turned out to explain in concrete terms what happens if that ruling stands. The RIAA, the National Music Publishers’ Association, and A2IM, which between them speak for most of the American music business, filed jointly. The international federations (IFPI, ICMP, FIAPF, and the International Video Federation) wrote to stress that this is the world’s problem, not just America’s. The Motion Picture Association weighed in on behalf of the major studios and streamers, and twenty IP law professors, including Mark Lemley, Pamela Samuelson, and Rebecca Tushnet, signed a brief led by Santa Clara’s Tyler Ochoa, who wrote his own volcanic takedown of the decision earlier this year. title: UN rights chief calls for impartial investigations amid election-related unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
content: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk on Friday urged calm and restraint amid escalating unrest ahead of regional elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, emphasizing the need for impartial investigations into protest-related deaths and renewed political dialogue to address longstanding grievances. Türk expressed concern over increasing violence in the region as tensions continue to rise before elections scheduled for July 27. He urged all parties to refrain from further escalation and emphasized that authorities must ensure security measures comply with international human rights standards, including respecting the rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression. The unrest centers upon the issue of 12 seats in the Legislative Assembly reserved for Kashmiri refugees who migrated to Pakistan following the 1947 partition and now reside outside Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The conflict between Pakistan and Kashmir stems from the 1947 partition of British India and a clash over control of the territory , which has resulted in decades of political instability, military conflicts, and widespread discrimination. The Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has led the demonstrations, argues that the arrangement allows Pakistan-based political parties to influence the region’s government while diverting development resources intended for residents of Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Last month, the region’s High Court ruled that the reserved seats are constitutionally protected and cannot be abolished without a constitutional amendment. The decision prompted the JAAC to intensify its protest campaign, arguing that the existing electoral framework undermines local representation and accountability. According to authorities, at least 28 people, including law enforcement officers, have been killed since protests began on June 4, while 79 others have been injured. title: UN: Djibouti faces severe food insecurity
content: The UN warned on Friday that Djibouti is facing severe, emergency-level hunger following the release of a report on the food insecurity situation. The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (ICP) Index’s report projected that between July and December 2026, more than 25 percent of Djibouti’s population, 256,000 people, are facing IPC Phase 3 or above (Crisis or worse), with “around 30,000 in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency).” The report identified “price shocks linked to import dependence,” “the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz,” “low purchasing power,” and “the effects of strong El Niño conditions” as factors linked to the worsening food insecurity crisis. The ICP also highlighted that refugees are the most impacted group. The ICP report warned that “urgent interventions are needed” to prevent further deterioration. These included anticipatory emergency responses, expansion of food and fund distribution to households most in need of assistance, protection of agropastoral livelihoods such as livestock and fishing against climate change impacts, and the scaling up of nutrition awareness. In June, the World Meteorological Organization warned that warm ocean waters are fueling the development of an El Niño event in June through August 2026. It highlighted that the Greater Horn of Africa, where Djibouti is situated, will experience “below-normal rainfall” during “the critical June-September rainy season.” Climate change has had a significant impact on vulnerable communities, and has been raised by the UN as a human rights issue. title: Rights group calls on member states to support African Court
content: Amnesty International on Friday urged member states of the African Union to continue providing political, legal, and financial support to the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights (African Court) to enable the court to carry out its mandate more effectively across the continent. In light of the court’s 20th anniversary, which fell on July 2, 2026, Japhet Biegon, the deputy regional director for East and Southern Africa at Amnesty International, emphasized how important it is now more than ever to provide continued support to the court. He stated: The African Court is an essential judicial avenue for individuals and civil society organizations who cannot obtain prompt, effective and adequate remedies for human rights violations in their own countries. Despite its challenges, the African Court has demonstrated dynamism and agility in examining the cases brought to it, developing strong jurisprudence and expanding the protection of human rights in Africa. The African Court was created in 2006 to provide a fully judicial body with the authority to deliver binding judgments on human rights violations, a monumental moment for the region since previous complaints were only handled by the African Commission , a quasi-judicial body. Proponents for the creation of the court hailed its establishment as a victory for African sovereignty, especially after a long colonial past. Today, human rights are rooted in the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) , which much of Africa was not a party to at the time due to colonization. Proponents have celebrated a homegrown judicial body that specifically caters to the needs of the African people without needing to be reliant on distant Eurocentric international bodies, ensuring that localized legal mechanisms understand the geopolitical realities of the African continent. title: Portugal legislation banning face coverings in public sparks criticism
content: Amnesty International on Friday condemned the Portuguese Parliament’s recent announcement that it passed a new law prohibiting the donning of face coverings in public areas, a decision that carries repercussions for fundamental civil liberties and individual autonomy in the country. J oão Godinho Martins, the executive director of Amnesty International in Portugal, stated: “Far from promoting women’s rights as claimed, this blanket ban is likely to have the opposite effect . Women who choose to wear full-face veils may face greater exclusion from public life, social isolation or increased difficulties in accessing education, employment and public services.” The announcement of the law is the latest development in a string of efforts in and around the European Union to curtail the usage of face coverings. The first draft of the bill, which the Portuguese Parliament approved on October 17, 2025, was the birthchild of the far-right Chega party, with the support of the ruling centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) and Liberal Initiative (IL). The original draft explicitly targeted Islamic garments such as the burqa and niqab. This was later revised to avoid total failure, however, in light of existing constitutional safeguards, such as the protection of freedom of religion under Article 41 of the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic. The final text imposed a universal ban on all forms of facial concealment in public spaces, and it is anchored in public security and public order, rather than having express provisions pinpointing that certain religious groups were banned from wearing them. However, Amnesty International pointed out that despite removing direct references to Muslim women, it will inevitably affect how they choose to express their religion and create a “neutrality trap” that disproportionately alienates a vulnerable minority. title: UK lord speaker warns rushed upper house reform risks losing constitutional safeguard
content: The UK lord speaker, Lord Forsyth of Drumlean, warned on Thursday that the rushed House of Lords reform could have the unintended effect of “blowing a constitutional fuse” in a public speech given at the Hansard Society . In his speech, Forsyth argued that the upper house can, without time constraints and pressures of re-elections, scrutinize legislation with expertise. He cited the house’s recent procurements of a ban on deepfake pornographic images ; an amendment that prevents journalists from being accidentally caught by the terrorism legislation; an under-16 social media ban ; an environmental regulation on sewage discharge into waterways; and progress on copyright protection for artificial intelligence developers. He said that the house is not the source of public dissatisfaction with politics. Forsyth also contended that appointments, rather than elections, of members in the upper house allow them to focus on legislative scrutiny instead of constituency work. He also raised concerns about elections for the upper house: if the election cycles of both houses synchronize, they mirror each other politically; if they are staggered, the houses led by opposing parties may result in regular gridlock akin to that of the US Congress. He proposed several changes to the formation of the upper house: lifting the limits on independent nominations and requiring the independent nominating body to ensure geographical balance and identify gaps in expertise when making the nominations. Currently, the House of Lords Appointments Commission appoints the vast majority of members; it attracts wide criticism for the upper house’s legitimacy in a democracy. title: Dr. Jill Lepore on why AI backlash is vital for the future
content: Today, I’m talking with Harvard professor and New Yorker staff writer Dr. Jill Lepore about her new book, The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State , which comes out on August 25. Jill is one of the best writers there is at identifying institutional patterns in history, and Decoder is a show about systems, so this book could not possibly be more in our zone.  You build systems by measuring things — gathering information, quantifying it as data, and taking action on it. And Jill’s big thesis in the book is that this kind of systemic measurement is really a dehumanizing act, one that flattens human concerns into something, well, artificial. These artificial structures touch everything — not just in the more obvious places like in apps or AI, but all the way up to politics and governance itself, and Jill’s insights here are a telling portrait of the way Big Tech and its billionaire figureheads have managed to break the very idea of the state itself.   Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts.
